recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Foundation — shared types, audit-log, leave-policy
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency modules first. shared-types owns LeaveType and LeaveStatus enums used by every other module. audit-log provides the GP-002 audit trail that all state-changing operations require. leave-policy defines the rules (max days, allowed types) that both leave-balance and leave-request consume.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: leave-balance
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on Phase 1 modules (shared-types, leave-policy, audit-log). Provides balance tracking, deduction, and credit operations that leave-request will call during apply/approve/reject flows.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: notification
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on Phase 1 modules (shared-types, audit-log). Provides notification dispatch that leave-request will call on state transitions. Can be built in parallel with Phase 2.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: leave-request (orchestration)
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on all prior phases. Orchestrates the full leave lifecycle: validates against policy, checks/deducts balances, records audits, dispatches notifications. This is the entry-point module that controllers/routes will call.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: shared-types (innermost, pure enums), audit-log (cross-cutting GP-002), leave-policy (business rules), leave-balance (state tracking), notification (side-effect dispatch), leave-request (orchestration, outermost application layer). All dependencies flow inward. Every service method is declared in an interface before implementation. No circular dependencies — verified. LeaveType and LeaveStatus enums placed in src/shared/types/ per the shared-value-type rule since they are pure data shapes used by multiple modules. One open question: balance deduction timing (application vs approval vs reservation) — recorded as openQuestion for the design agent.

open_questions.question: When should leave balance be deducted — at application time or at approval time?
open_questions.impact: Affects applyLeave (whether it deducts or only validates), approveLeave (whether it deducts or confirms a prior deduction), rejectLeave (whether it credits back), and cancelLeave (whether it credits back). The choice determines the transactional boundary and the meaning of "available balance" shown to employees.
candidate_options: Deduct at application: applyLeave deducts immediately; rejectLeave and cancelLeave credit back. Balance reflects committed + remaining.
Deduct at approval: applyLeave only validates sufficient balance; approveLeave performs the deduction. Balance reflects only approved usage.
Reservation model: applyLeave creates a hold (reserved balance); approveLeave converts hold to deduction; rejectLeave/cancelLeave release the hold.
